questions.stem: Suppose the student union of your university is organizing an online discussion on interpersonal relationships. You are to write an essay on ways to maintain a warm and friendly relationship with your classmates and on the benefits of such a relationship. You will have 30 minutes f or the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words .
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
A warm and friendly relationship plays an important part in our campus life. Since we spend most of our time with classmates, it is worth thinking about how to maintain such a relationship and what benefits it can bring.

There are several practical ways to keep such a relationship close. First, we should communicate sincerely. For example, when a misunderstanding happens, we can simply talk it over honestly instead of staying cold. Besides, it also helps to support each other in study and daily life. When a classmate misses a lecture, sharing our notes and showing respect for different habits can quickly bring us closer.

As a result, such a relationship can bring us real benefits. It eases our pressure when courses get hard, pushes us to make progress together, and creates a strong sense of belonging in class. In short, building such warm bonds with our classmates is well worth our effort throughout the precious college years.

transcript.text: Police have reported a man being bitten by a 4-foot snake when he lifted his toilet seat on Sunday morning.
transcript.zh: 警方报告称,周日早晨一名男子在掀开马桶盖时被一条4英尺长的蛇咬伤。

transcript.text: The snake was not poisonous, so the man did not have to go to the hospital, but his arm was medically treated at the scene.
transcript.zh: 这条蛇没有毒性,因此该男子无需前往医院,但他的手臂在现场接受了医疗处理。

transcript.text: The police officer interviewed told news reporters the snake didn't belong to the man and it was unclear how it got into the apartment.
transcript.zh: 接受采访的警官告诉新闻记者,这条蛇不属于该男子,目前尚不清楚它是如何进入公寓的。

transcript.text: The snake was eventually captured by the local animal handlers and taken to an animal hospital afterward. It was being treated for an outer skin infection. It was unclear who the owner was. The snake may be taken to a local zoo for care if the owner does not come forward.
transcript.zh: 这条蛇最终被当地动物处理人员捕获,随后被送往动物医院。它正在接受外层皮肤感染的治疗。目前尚不清楚主人是谁。如果主人不出现认领,这条蛇可能会被送到当地动物园照料。

transcript.text: Over the years, other creatures like frogs and fish have found their way into toilets. But this was the first instance of a snake in recent years.
transcript.zh: 多年来,青蛙和鱼等其他生物也曾以各种方式进入马桶。但这是近年来首次出现蛇的情况。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the police report?

options.text: A man was bitten by a snake.
A man was taken to a hospital.
A man kept a 4-foot snake as a pet.
A man fell off his toilet seat.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Police have reported a man being bitten by a 4-foot snake when he lifted his toilet seat on Sunday morning.信号：新闻导语句即答案 。答案句就是 Police have reported a man being bitten by a 4-foot snake when he lifted his toilet seat on …

optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：录音第二段明确说 the man did not have to go to the hospital——这位男子**没有**去医院，只是在现场处理了手臂。选项 A man was taken to a hospital. 盗用了原文的 hospital 一词却把否定砍掉，反成肯定，是典型"听到 hospital 就想选"的陷阱。 借用原文：a 4-foot snake
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 A man kept a 4-foot snake as a pet. 把录音第 1 段里的 a 4-foot snake 原词搬过来，看似耳熟。但录音第 3 段明确说 the snake didn't belong to the man，蛇并不是男子的，更谈不上 kept…as a pet。这是"听到原词就想选"的原词陷阱。 借用原文：he lifted his toilet seat
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 A man fell off his toilet seat. 借用了录音 he lifted his toilet seat 中的 toilet seat 这块"熟面孔"，但把动作偷换成了 fell off（从马桶上摔下来）。录音说的是"他掀开马桶盖"，根本没说他摔倒。这又是一处原词陷阱叠加偷换概念。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a man being bitten by a 4-foot snake ↔ A man was bitten by a snake. 非谓语转过去时·同义直接对应）

questions.evidenceText: Police have reported a man being bitten by a 4-foot snake when he lifted his toilet seat on Sunday morning.

questions.stem: What does the report say was still unclear?

options.text: Where the snake had been taken.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：It was unclear who the owner was. The snake may be taken to a local zoo for care if the owner does not come forward.信号：unclear + who 直接锁定 。答案信号是 It was unclear who the owner was. 中的 unclear 一词——它与题干 still unclear 直接对应；unclear 后…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音 The snake was eventually captured by the local animal handlers and taken to an animal hospital afterward. 已经明确告诉我们蛇被送去了 animal hospital；之后还补了一句若无主认领"可能送到当地动物园"，去向并非"unclear"。选项 Where the snake had been taken. 借用 taken 这一原词制造"哪里去了仍不清楚"的错觉，实际录音对去向已交代。 借用原文：It was being treated for an outer skin infection.
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音 It was being treated for an outer skin infection. 明确说蛇正在因外皮感染接受治疗，感染状况已确认而非未明。选项 Whether the snake was infected. 把 infection 一词盗作诱饵，骗"听到 infection 就想选"的考生。 借用原文：The snake was eventually captured by the local animal handlers
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音 The snake was eventually captured by the local animal handlers 明确说蛇是被当地的"动物管理员"捕获的，捕获方式（由谁、怎么抓）已交代。选项 How the snake was captured. 直接挪用 captured 一词，把已说清的事伪装成 unclear，是经典原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（It was unclear who the owner was. ↔ Who owned the snake. 名词转动词·who 从句同义重写）

transcript.text: Every week since last April, Andrea Belcher has been doing something slightly unusual and amusing when she takes out her trash.
transcript.zh: 自去年四月以来,每周当Andrea Belcher倒垃圾时,她都会做一件略显不寻常而有趣的事。

transcript.text: It all started off when a movie star shared a photo of herself putting her trash bins out in a ball gown. This inspired Andrea to get dressed up to take out the trash.
transcript.zh: 这一切始于一位电影明星分享了一张自己穿着晚礼服倒垃圾的照片。这启发了Andrea盛装打扮去倒垃圾。

transcript.text: She was too embarrassed to do it during the day. So one dark evening, she put on her black off-the-shoulder gown and put her trash bin out. Her daughter filmed it and the whole family laughed, but it seemed to go down well.
transcript.zh: 她白天不好意思这样做。所以在一个漆黑的夜晚,她穿上了黑色露肩礼服去倒垃圾桶。她女儿拍摄了这一幕,全家人都笑了,但效果似乎不错。

transcript.text: The following weeks, she found other outfits in her dressing-up box, and dressed up as different characters and famous people, sharing her exploits on social media. Before long, people started offering up their own fancy dresses for her to wear. And before she knew it, she had done 20 weeks.
transcript.zh: 接下来的几周,她从自己的装扮箱里找出其他服装,打扮成不同的角色和名人,在社交媒体上分享她的趣事。不久之后,人们开始主动提供自己的华丽服装给她穿。在她意识到之前,她已经坚持了20周。

transcript.text: Explaining why she has kept up the videos, Andrea explained how nice it was to have a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile. Besides, it also helps to remind people in the community to put out their trash bins each week.
transcript.zh: 在解释为什么她一直坚持拍摄这些视频时, Andrea说能有一点乐趣和疯狂让人们微笑是多么美好。此外,这也有助于提醒社区里的人们每周倒垃圾桶。

questions.stem: What has Andrea Belcher been doing since last April?

options.text: Taking her trash out in fancy dresses.
Amusing herself by going to ball parties.
Sharing her photos with famous movie stars.
Posting her daughter's photos on social media.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Every week since last April, Andrea Belcher has been doing something slightly unusual and amusing when she takes out her trash.信号：开篇点题句 + 时间状语锁定 。新闻开篇 Every week since last April 与题干 since last April 完全对应，时间状语就是答案信号；后半句 when she takes out…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音第2段提到 a movie star shared a photo of herself putting her trash bins out in a ball gown，ball gown（晚礼服）只是她穿的衣服样式，并不是说"她去参加舞会"。选项 B 把 ball 偷换成 ball parties，把"穿礼服倒垃圾"硬扭成"去舞会自娱"，是典型的原词陷阱。 借用原文：a movie star shared a photo of herself putting her trash bins out in a ball gown
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：录音第2段明确 a movie star shared a photo of herself putting her trash bins out in a ball gown——分享照片的人是那位明星，分享的内容是明星自己的照片。选项 C 把动作主语换成了 Andrea，把"她和明星分享照片"安到她头上，是张冠李戴。 借用原文：Her daughter filmed it
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：录音第3段说 Her daughter filmed it，是女儿帮她拍视频；第4段说 sharing her exploits on social media，分享的是"她自己的事迹"。选项 D 却说"发布她女儿的照片"，把"女儿帮拍"偷换成"发布女儿的照片"，主客颠倒。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（doing something slightly unusual and amusing when she takes out her trash ↔ Taking her trash out in fancy dresses 概括 + 后文具体细化）

questions.evidenceText: Every week since last April, Andrea Belcher has been doing something slightly unusual and amusing when she takes out her trash.

questions.stem: Why has Andrea Belcher kept up her videos?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：Explaining why she has kept up the videos, Andrea explained how nice it was to have a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile.信号：结尾解释句直接对应题干 。录音第5段开头 Explaining why she has kept up the videos 与题干 Why has Andrea Belcher kept up her videos…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：录音里完全没有出现 popular/famous 类的动机描述；她坚持的原因被明确说成 to have a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile，与"让自己出名"无关。选项 A 是"花絮新闻最常见的诱选动机"——预读时已警惕。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音第3段有 Her daughter filmed it and the whole family laughed，daughter 真的被念到，但只是说女儿帮她拍、全家笑——这不是她坚持的目的。选项 C 把 daughter 偷过来，硬安成"为了讨女儿欢心"，是典型原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：录音里既没有 record（记录）也没有 achievements（成就）类的表达；she had done 20 weeks 只是叙述事实，并非"为了记录成就"。选项 D 是凭"长期坚持"脑补出来的，与解释信号后给出的真实动机不符。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile ↔ To amuse people made people smile = amuse people）

questions.evidenceText: Explaining why she has kept up the videos, Andrea explained how nice it was to have a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile.

transcript.text: No money but still hungry? No problem! Welcome to Frank's restaurant where customers are paying for meals and leaving receipts on a board. Anyone who is hungry and wants something to eat can take one, no questions asked and hand it to the staff for some food.
transcript.zh: 没钱但仍然饿着？没问题！欢迎来到Frank's餐厅，这里的顾客为餐食付款后会把收据留在一块板子上。任何饿了想吃东西的人都可以拿走一张，无需回答任何问题，然后把它交给工作人员换取食物。

transcript.text: The idea for the board of free meals started after a donor came in with $100 for each member of its staff. After two staffers returned to their share, there was $700 leftover according to Tarah Morris, the owner of the restaurant, so they decided to do something more by creating the board.
transcript.zh: 免费餐食板的想法始于一位捐赠者带着100美元来给每位员工。据餐厅老板Tarah Morris说,两名员工退还了他们的份额后,还剩下700美元,于是他们决定通过创建这块板子来做更多的事情。

transcript.text: The board of free meals inside the restaurant shows a host of potential meals already paid for by customers, each costing about $10. The board has messages of kindness like, "If you want more kindness in the world, put it here."
transcript.zh: 餐厅内的免费餐食板展示着许多已由顾客付款的潜在餐食,每份约10美元。板子上有善意的留言,比如"如果你想让世界有更多善意,就把它放在这里。"

transcript.text: The drive has been going on for two weeks and Morris said just under 50 customers have picked up a free meal. There have been no reports of anyone taking advantage of the situation. In fact, there are a lot more people giving tickets than receiving. It seems people want to help and are driven by helping others.
transcript.zh: 这项活动已经进行了两周, Morris说有将近50位顾客领取了免费餐食。没有任何人利用这种情况的报告。事实上,给予餐券的人比领取的人多得多。似乎人们想要帮助他人,并被帮助他人所驱动。

questions.stem: What can people do at Frank's restaurant?

options.text: Eat as much as they want for $10.
Have a chance of winning a $100 prize.
Have a meal even if they have no money.
Get a free meal after answering some questions.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：No money but still hungry? No problem! Welcome to Frank's restaurant where customers are paying for meals and leaving receipts on a board. Anyone who is hungry and wants something to eat can take one, no questions asked and hand it to the staff for some food.信号：导语句直接点题 。开头连用两个设问 No money but still hungry? No problem!，紧接着用 Welcome to… 引出餐厅做法，这是新闻典型的导语式信号——把整则新闻的核心事实押在第…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音第三段确实提到每份饭 each costing about $10，但说的是每张小票背后对应的餐费，并非顾客只要付 $10 就能 Eat as much as they want；选项盗用 $10 这个原词，把它扭成自助式的随便吃，是典型的听到数字就想选式陷阱。 借用原文：a donor came in with $100 for each member of its staff
optionAnalysis.B: 录音第二段说 a donor came in with $100 for each member of its staff，$100 是某位捐赠者发给员工的人均款项，根本不是 a $100 prize 抽奖奖金；选项盗用 $100 这个原词，再嫁接 prize 制造抽奖联想。 借用原文：no questions asked
optionAnalysis.D: 录音里 no questions asked 明确说取餐时不需要回答任何问题，而 Get a free meal after answering some questions 偏偏要求顾客 answering some questions 才能得到免费餐，与原文方向相反；选项盗用 questions 这个原词，却反转了它的语义。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（No money but still hungry? No problem! ↔ even if they have no money 设问反问 = 让步条件）

transcript.text: W: Welcome to our program, Friends and Relationships. Our guest today is psychologist Steve Pinker from McGill University.
transcript.zh: W: 欢迎来到我们的节目《朋友与关系》。我们今天的嘉宾是来自McGill大学的心理学家Steve Pinker。

transcript.text: M: Glad to be here, Jane.
transcript.zh: M: 很高兴来到这里, Jane。

transcript.text: W: Hi, Steve. Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear. They may block us on their social media accounts and stop responding to our emails. They simply vanish without a trace.
transcript.zh: W: 你好, Steve。我们今天的问题是为什么朋友会突然消失。他们可能会在社交媒体账号上屏蔽我们,不再回复我们的邮件。他们就这样消失得无影无踪。

transcript.text: M: The answer may lie in childhood, the way the person related to their mom and dad. It's related to their attachment styles.
transcript.zh: M: 答案可能在于童年时期,也就是这个人与父母相处的方式。这与他们的依恋类型有关。

transcript.text: W: Attachment styles?
transcript.zh: W: 依恋类型?

transcript.text: M: Yeah. There are two different attachment styles: an anxious attachment style and an avoidant attachment style. When there is a relationship breakdown with their parents, children with an anxious attachment style scream and cry to get their parents to come back. But other children simply shut down and try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation. And these attachment styles carry on into adulthood.
transcript.zh: M: 是的。有两种不同的依恋类型:焦虑型依恋和回避型依恋。当与父母的关系破裂时,焦虑型依恋的孩子会又哭又闹,想让父母回来。但另一些孩子只是封闭自己,试图通过忽视这种情况来处理自己的情绪。而这些依恋类型会延续到成年期。

transcript.text: W: Does avoidance reduce their stress levels?
transcript.zh: W: 回避能降低他们的压力水平吗?

transcript.text: M: Not really. Their stress levels are actually the same as those experienced by the children who yell and scream.
transcript.zh: M: 并不能。他们的压力水平实际上和那些大喊大叫的孩子经历的压力水平是一样的。

transcript.text: W: And I assume both might be termed insecure.
transcript.zh: W: 我猜这两种都可以被称为不安全型。

transcript.text: M: Exactly. And it's a very insecure attachment.
transcript.zh: M: 完全正确。这是一种非常不安全的依恋。

transcript.text: W: How does an insecure attachment affect relationships between friends, co-workers and romantic relationships?
transcript.zh: W: 不安全型依恋如何影响朋友之间、同事之间以及恋爱关系?

transcript.text: M: It's the same as conflicts. So if you have a disagreement with a securely attached person, they're not going to panic. They're able to hear what the other person is saying and express their own feelings and thoughts effectively. However, an insecurely attached person won't. They might either attack you, get defensive, or just disappear from your life. To them, a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship.
transcript.zh: M: 和冲突的情况一样。所以如果你和一个安全型依恋的人产生分歧,他们不会惊慌失措。他们能够听进对方在说什么,并有效地表达自己的感受和想法。然而,不安全型依恋的人不会这样。他们可能会攻击你,变得防御性很强,或者直接从你的生活中消失。对他们来说,分歧,无论在你眼中多么微小,都预示着关系的终结。

transcript.text: W: That explains why they suddenly disappear.
transcript.zh: W: 这就解释了为什么他们会突然消失。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man?

options.text: He is a host for a TV program.
He is a primary school teacher.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Welcome to our program, Friends and Relationships. Our guest today is psychologist Steve Pinker from McGill University.信号：开场介绍嘉宾的固定句 。信号词是 Our guest today is psychologist——「今天的嘉宾是…」是访谈节目报身份的标志句，紧跟其后的名词就是嘉宾职业。

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音通篇没有提到男士是作家，He is a famous writer. 属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音里 Welcome to our program 中的 program 确实是「节目」原词，He is a host for a TV program. 故意用 program 引诱，但说「欢迎收看节目」的是女主持人 Jane，男士是「嘉宾」(guest)，不是主持人。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：录音从头到尾未提及小学/教师/teach 等任何线索，He is a primary school teacher. 属于完全无中生有。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（psychologist Steve Pinker ↔ He is a psychologist. 同词直给——但听清职业）

questions.evidenceText: Welcome to our program, Friends and Relationships. Our guest today is psychologist Steve Pinker from McGill University.

questions.stem: What are the speakers mainly talking about?

options.text: Why social media accounts vanish without a trace.
Why parents raise their children in different ways.
Why people fail to respond to emails promptly.
Why friends break off contact all of a sudden.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P3）：Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear. They may block us on their social media accounts and stop responding to our emails. They simply vanish without a trace.信号：Our question today is… 是节目抛题信号 。信号词是 Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear——访谈节目用 Our questio…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Why social media accounts vanish without a trace. 抠走了录音里的 social media accounts 和 vanish without a trace 两个原词，听到就想选；但录音说的是「朋友」会通过拉黑社交账号等方式消失，主体是「朋友」，不是「账号本身」——选项把「朋友消失」的一种具体表现错读成了主题，属以偏概全。 借用原文：The answer may lie in childhood
optionAnalysis.B: 录音确实在 The answer may lie in childhood, the way the person related to their mom and dad. 谈到了童年与父母关系，但那是嘉宾对「为什么朋友会突然消失」的解释；选项 Why parents raise their children in different ways. 把这个解释方向错抬成了主题，主题是「消失」不是「育儿方式」。 借用原文：stop responding to our emails
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：Why people fail to respond to emails promptly. 抠走了录音原词 stop responding to our emails，但「不回邮件」只是「朋友消失」的一种具体形态而已，把它当主题同样是以偏概全，且和 A 犯一样的错。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（why friends suddenly disappear ↔ Why friends break off contact all of a sudden. 同义改写——disappear ↔ break off contact，suddenly ↔ all of a sudden）

questions.evidenceText: Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear. They may block us on their social media accounts and stop responding to our emails. They simply vanish without a trace.

questions.stem: How do children with an anxious attachment style react to a breakdown in their relationship with parents?

options.text: They scream to get their parents back.
They attempt to ignore the whole situation.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：When there is a relationship breakdown with their parents, children with an anxious attachment style scream and cry to get their parents to come back. But other children simply shut down and try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation.信号：对照结构 anxious …. But other children … 。信号词是 But other children——嘉宾用 But 把两类孩子的反应并排对照。这种对照句是出题铁矿，正确反应几乎都在 But …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：They simply shut themselves down. 抠走了录音原词 simply shut down，听到 simply shut down 就想选；但录音明确说这是 But other children(另一类，即回避型)的反应，不是焦虑型的反应。 借用原文：try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation
optionAnalysis.B: They avoid showing their emotions. 描述的是「回避情绪」，更接近回避型(But other children…try to deal with their emotions by ignoring)；焦虑型 scream and cry 反而是大力外露情绪，与本选项相反。 借用原文：try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：They attempt to ignore the whole situation. 抠走的是录音原词 ignoring the situation，听到就想选；但这同样是 But other children 那一类(回避型)的反应，不是焦虑型的反应。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（scream and cry to get their parents to come back ↔ They scream to get their parents back. 选项几乎是原句裁剪）

questions.evidenceText: When there is a relationship breakdown with their parents, children with an anxious attachment style scream and cry to get their parents to come back. But other children simply shut down and try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation.

questions.stem: What does the man say about insecurely attached people?

options.text: They may regard any difference as the end of a relationship.
They are on better terms with friends and romantic partners.
They try to express their feelings and thoughts effectively.
They attach more value to their relationships with others.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：However, an insecurely attached person won't. They might either attack you, get defensive, or just disappear from your life. To them, a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship.信号：However + To them 双重信号锁定结论 。信号词一：However, an insecurely attached person won't——However 是转折信号，前面说安全型怎么处理，转折后才…

optionAnalysis.B: They are on better terms with friends and romantic partners. 是正面描述「和朋友/恋人相处更好」，但录音里嘉宾对不安全型的描述是 They might either attack you, get defensive, or just disappear from your life.，是关系处理失败的方向，选项与录音方向完全相反。 借用原文：They're able to hear what the other person is saying and express their own feelings and thoughts effectively.
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：They try to express their feelings and thoughts effectively. 抠走的是录音原词 express their own feelings and thoughts effectively，听到 express…effectively 就想选；但这句话是嘉宾对 securely attached(安全型)人的描述，不是问的不安全型。
optionAnalysis.D: They attach more value to their relationships with others. 说「他们更看重关系」，录音通篇没有这种说法。相反，录音说他们把小分歧当作关系终结的信号，是「轻易抛弃关系」的方向，不是「更看重关系」。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（To them, a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship. ↔ They may regard any difference as the end of a relationship. 同义改写——signals ↔ regard…as，no matter how small ↔ any）

questions.evidenceText: However, an insecurely attached person won't. They might either attack you, get defensive, or just disappear from your life. To them, a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship.

transcript.text: M: I hear you're going to Japan soon.
transcript.zh: M: 我听说你快要去日本了。

transcript.text: W: Yes, that's right.
transcript.zh: W: 是的，没错。

transcript.text: M: Could I ask you a favor?
transcript.zh: M: 我能请你帮个忙吗？

transcript.text: W: Sure. What is it?
transcript.zh: W: 当然可以。什么事？

transcript.text: M: I was wondering if you could get me some jeans while you're there. I'll pay you back, of course.
transcript.zh: M: 我在想你在那儿的时候能不能帮我买条牛仔裤。当然我会还你钱的。

transcript.text: W: A pair of jeans? Okay. I don't see why not. But what's wrong with jeans here?
transcript.zh: W: 一条牛仔裤？好吧。我觉得没问题。但这里的牛仔裤有什么不好吗？

transcript.text: M: Well, I just love good jeans and Japan happens to make the best in the world. My friend brought me a pair from there five years ago, and they still look new.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯，我就是喜欢好牛仔裤，而日本恰好生产世界上最好的牛仔裤。我朋友五年前从那儿给我带了一条，现在看起来还跟新的一样。

transcript.text: W: Really? I had no idea Japan made jeans. I would have thought America made the best jeans because it's a typical American garment.
transcript.zh: W: 真的吗？我完全不知道日本还生产牛仔裤。我还以为美国生产最好的牛仔裤呢，因为这是典型的美国服装。

transcript.text: M: Yeah, I thought so too. But it turns out Japan still has some very old mills with the traditional weaving tools used to make jeans the original way. It's a slower process of making clothing. But the end result is surely superior. Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural. They have a denser weave, and are more durable than any other jeans in the world.
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，我也是这么想的。但事实证明日本仍然有一些非常古老的工厂，使用传统的织布工具以原始方式制作牛仔裤。这是一种比较慢的服装制作工艺。但最终成品绝对更优质。而且，他们使用的面料质量更高，染料也是天然的。织得更密实，比世界上任何其他牛仔裤都更耐用。

transcript.text: W: That sounds cool. What size do you want and how much are they?
transcript.zh: W: 听起来不错。你要什么尺码的，多少钱？

transcript.text: M: I have a 34 waist and size 30 or 32 in length. Either is fine. They should be around $500. But make double certain they are made in Japan.
transcript.zh: M: 我腰围34，长度30或32都行。哪个都可以。大概500美元左右。但一定要再三确认是日本制造的。

transcript.text: W: $500? Boy, that's expensive. Do you typically spend that much on a pair of casual trousers?
transcript.zh: W: 500美元？天哪，太贵了。你平时买休闲裤都花这么多钱吗？

transcript.text: M: They are a little pricey, yes. But they are very special. Bear in mind, they will last me several years and they're very fashionable too. I think they're totally worth it.
transcript.zh: M: 确实是有点贵。但它们很特别。要知道，它们能穿好几年，而且也很时尚。我觉得完全值得。

questions.stem: What makes the man choose to buy jeans made in Japan?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural. They have a denser weave, and are more durable than any other jeans in the world.信号：比较级 higher / denser / more durable 集中爆发 。the fabric they use is of a higher quality 与 more durable than any …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：原文 They should be around $500. 提到了具体价格，让粗心的考生听到数字就奔『price』；但价格出现在男士交代规格那段，根本不是他选择日本货的『理由』，男士选日本货的理由集中在第 9 段的质量描述，Their price. 是典型原词陷阱。 借用原文：they're very fashionable too
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：全文没有出现任何关于 color 的描述，Their color. 属于无中生有；它和 quality/design 一样是『物品属性词』，被列在这里只为凑成四项并列结构干扰考生。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：原文末段 they're very fashionable too 与 But they are very special 容易让人联想到『款式好』而选 Their design.；但 fashionable/special 在原文里是男士补充说明价格值不值时的次要修饰，不是他选『日本货』的核心理由——核心理由是第 9 段集中讲的质量。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the fabric they use is of a higher quality ↔ Their quality. 原文 higher quality 直接对应选项 quality）

questions.evidenceText: Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural. They have a denser weave, and are more durable than any other jeans in the world.

questions.stem: Why is the woman puzzled by the man's request?

options.text: Jeans are a typical American garment.
America makes the best-known brands of jeans.
America has the best weaving tools in the world.
Jeans are available in a greater variety in America.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：Really? I had no idea Japan made jeans. I would have thought America made the best jeans because it's a typical American garment.信号：心理动词过去式 had no idea / would have thought 。I had no idea Japan made jeans 与 I would have thought America made…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：原文 I would have thought America made the best jeans 与 more durable than any other jeans in the world 都出现了 best 类用语，容易误导考生选含 best-known 的 America makes the best-known brands of jeans.；但女士原话说的是 best jeans（最好的牛仔裤），不是 best-known brands（最知名的品牌），后者是偷换概念。 借用原文：Japan still has some very old mills with the traditional weaving tools
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：原文 Japan still has some very old mills with the traditional weaving tools 说的是『日本』有传统织布工具，America has the best weaving tools in the world. 把这条属性硬安到 America 头上，是典型张冠李戴；同时女士困惑的依据也不是『美国有最好的织布工具』，而是『牛仔裤是美国典型服饰』。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：原文从未做过『美国牛仔裤种类比日本多』的比较，Jeans are available in a greater variety in America. 凭空造出 greater variety 这一比较，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（it's a typical American garment ↔ Jeans are a typical American garment. 代词 it 还原为 jeans 后字面等同）

questions.evidenceText: Really? I had no idea Japan made jeans. I would have thought America made the best jeans because it's a typical American garment.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the dyes of Japanese jeans?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural.信号：dyes are natural 是关键词后直接表语 。the dyes are natural——题干关键词 dyes 在原文里只出现一次，紧跟 are + 形容词 natural，完全是『关键词原句锁定 + 表语…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：They are artificial. 是 the dyes are natural 的直接反义，原文明确说染料是天然的，artificial 与之极性相反，属于反向干扰。 借用原文：But the end result is surely superior.
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问：原文整段 9 强调日本牛仔裤独特优良（traditional weaving tools / superior / denser weave），容易让人选 They are unique.；但题干特定问 dyes，原文给的形容词是 natural，unique 是把『整段对日本牛仔裤的整体评价』错位安到 dyes 头上。 借用原文：But they are very special.
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：原文 But they are very special. 中的 special 形容的是『日本牛仔裤这件物品』，不是 dyes；They are special. 把整体的 special 嫁接到了局部 dyes 上，与 C 同类错法。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the dyes are natural ↔ They are natural. 原词复现下的指代还原）

questions.evidenceText: Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality and the dyes are natural.

questions.stem: What does the man say about Japanese jeans at the end of the conversation?
questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P13）：They are a little pricey, yes. But they are very special. Bear in mind, they will last me several years and they're very fashionable too. I think they're totally worth it.信号：让步 but + 下结论 I think…totally worth it 。They are a little pricey, yes. But they are very special. 是让步转折，I thi…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：原文 Do you typically spend that much on a pair of casual trousers? 里 casual 出现在女士的反问中，并非男士对 Japanese jeans 的表态；They are for casual wearing. 直接搬走 casual 一词制造熟悉感，但题干特定问『男士说』，casual 不是男士的观点。 借用原文：They are a little pricey, yes.
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：原文从未提到日本牛仔裤『在男生中流行』，They are popular with boys. 完全是从『jeans 这种衣物大众印象=年轻男孩穿的』的常识跳过来的，与录音内容无关。
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：原文 They are a little pricey, yes. 确实承认贵，They are much too pricey. 把这句话强化为『贵得过分』；但男士紧跟一个 But 把态度翻到 totally worth it，C 只取了让步前半、丢了真意。much too pricey 的『过分嫌贵』也与男士的 a little pricey + 值得相矛盾。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I think they're totally worth it. ↔ They are worth the price. totally worth it 与 worth the price 同义）

questions.evidenceText: They are a little pricey, yes. But they are very special. Bear in mind, they will last me several years and they're very fashionable too. I think they're totally worth it.

transcript.text: Every time I walk out of a superhero movie, I feel the same way. I experience a sense of longing, realizing that there should be more in life. The desire for adventure is a human one. Superhero films capture this desire perfectly.
transcript.zh: 每次走出超级英雄电影院，我都有同样的感受。我体验到一种渴望感，意识到生活中应该有更多东西。对冒险的渴望是人类共有的。超级英雄电影完美地捕捉了这种渴望。

transcript.text: The plot of each superhero film has become relatively predictable: the world is in peril, the world needs a hero, the hero is in peril, the hero resolves the peril, the hero saves the world. Each film has an attractive lead, several expensive explosions, a few jokes to lighten the mood, and numerous punches that land unrealistically well. Even though we basically know what will happen, we keep coming back for more.
transcript.zh: 每部超级英雄电影的情节都变得相对可预测：世界陷入危险，世界需要英雄，英雄陷入危险，英雄化解危险，英雄拯救世界。每部电影都有一个有魅力的主角、几场昂贵的爆炸、一些缓和气氛的笑话，以及无数不切实际地精准命中的拳头。尽管我们基本上知道会发生什么，我们还是不断回来观看更多。

transcript.text: The elites of our society have rejected superhero films. They say the films lack any form of artistry. These movies are criticized as being too simple. But they give the fans what they want—entertainment.
transcript.zh: 我们社会的精英阶层排斥超级英雄电影。他们说这些电影缺乏任何形式的艺术性。这些电影被批评为过于简单。但它们给粉丝想要的东西——娱乐。

transcript.text: No matter the form in which they reveal themselves, hero stories will always be present in life. It's not just about being entertained, but also being inspired. One author has mentioned that women desire to play an irreplaceable role in a great adventure. "Most young women want to be a part of something grand, something important." It seems clear that this principle applies to men, as well.
transcript.zh: 无论以何种形式呈现，英雄故事将始终存在于生活中。这不仅关乎娱乐，也关乎激励。一位作者曾提到，女性渴望在一场伟大的冒险中扮演不可替代的角色。"大多数年轻女性想成为宏大事物、重要事物的一部分。"这一原则显然也适用于男性。

transcript.text: So next time you see your favorite superhero film, be entertained, but also be inspired. Let that small longing you feel motivate you to make a difference.
transcript.zh: 所以下次你观看最喜欢的超级英雄电影时，享受娱乐，但也要受到激励。让你感受到的那种微小渴望激励你去做出改变。

questions.stem: How does the speaker feel every time he walks out of a superhero movie?

options.text: He wants to see it again.
He feels as inspired as other audience members.
He longs to become a superstar himself.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Every time I walk out of a superhero movie, I feel the same way. I experience a sense of longing, realizing that there should be more in life.信号：题干与原文几乎同句开篇 。Every time I walk out of a superhero movie, I feel the same way. 这句与题干 every time he walks out …

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：He wants to see it again. 原文从头到尾没说“想再看一遍”，only 说每次走出影院都有同样的感受——这是把“every time（每次都）”误读成了“want to see again（想再看）”。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：He feels as inspired as other audience members. 盗用了原文 being inspired 这个词，但原文是说“hero stories 让人 inspired”是普遍道理，且根本没说“和其他观众一样被启发”——加了“as … as other audience members”这层比较，是凭空添料。 借用原文：I experience a sense of longing
optionAnalysis.D: He longs to become a superstar himself. 用了 longs 这个 long 的近义动词来引诱，但原文只说“渴望生活里有更多东西”，从未说“渴望自己也成为超级巨星”——这是把抽象的“渴望”过度具体化成“想当超级巨星”。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a sense of longing ↔ desires longing 与 desire 同义）

questions.evidenceText: Every time I walk out of a superhero movie, I feel the same way. I experience a sense of longing, realizing that there should be more in life.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the plot of all superhero movies?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The plot of each superhero film has become relatively predictable: the world is in peril, the world needs a hero, the hero is in peril, the hero resolves the peril, the hero saves the world.信号：题干关键词 plot 原词复现 + 冒号定义式说明 。The plot of each superhero film has become relatively predictable 里 plot 与题干 the …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：It is rather unrealistic. 盗用了原文 numerous punches that land unrealistically well 里的 unrealistically，但原文说的是“拳头打得不真实”，是描写动作镜头，不是说整个 plot（剧情）不现实——把局部修饰偷换成整体判断。 借用原文：They say the films lack any form of artistry.

optionAnalysis.C: It is somewhat complicated. 与原文判断方向相反——第 3 段 These movies are criticized as being too simple. 明说被批评为 too simple（太简单），与 complicated（复杂）完全对立。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：They are biased against women. 盗用了原文 women desire to play an irreplaceable role 里的 women 一词，但第 4 段是作者引用作家观点说“女性想参与伟大冒险”，跟精英的看法毫无关系；且原文从未说电影“对女性有偏见”。

transcript.text: Telling stories is one of the most powerful means leaders have to influence, teach and inspire. Storytelling forges connections among people. When it comes to our countries, our communities, and our families, we understand instinctively that the stories we hold in common are an important part of the ties that bind.
transcript.zh: 讲故事是领导者用来影响、教导和激励他人的最有力手段之一。讲故事能在人与人之间建立联系。当涉及我们的国家、我们的社区和我们的家庭时,我们本能地理解,我们共同拥有的故事是维系彼此纽带的重要组成部分。

transcript.text: This understanding also holds true in the business world, where an organization's stories, and the stories its leaders tell, help solidify relationships in a way that factual statements don't.
transcript.zh: 这种理解在商业世界中同样适用,在那里,一个组织的故事以及其领导者讲述的故事,能以一种事实陈述所无法做到的方式帮助巩固关系。

transcript.text: Good stories do more than create a sense of connection. They build familiarity and trust. They allow the listener to enter the story, making them more open to learning. Good stories can contain multiple meanings, so they're surprisingly economical in conveying complex ideas in graspable ways. And stories are more engaging than the recital of data points or a discussion of abstract ideas.
transcript.zh: 好的故事不仅仅能创造一种联系感。它们建立熟悉感和信任。它们让听众进入故事之中,使他们更愿意学习。好的故事可以包含多重含义,因此它们在以可理解的方式传达复杂思想方面出人意料地经济高效。而且故事比罗列数据点或讨论抽象概念更具吸引力。

transcript.text: Stories about professional mistakes and what leaders learned from them are another great avenue for learning. Because people identify so closely with stories, they can imagine how they would have acted in similar circumstances. They're able to work through situations in a way that's risk-free. There are extra benefits for leaders: with a simple personal story, they can convey fundamental values. They can offer insight into the evolution of their own experience and knowledge, presenting themselves as more approachable and then they are more likely to inspire others to want to know more.
transcript.zh: 关于职业错误以及领导者从中学到的经验的故事是另一条很好的学习途径。因为人们与故事产生如此紧密的认同,他们可以想象自己在类似情况下会如何行动。他们能够以一种零风险的方式来处理各种情境。对领导者来说还有额外的好处:通过一个简单的个人故事,他们可以传达基本价值观。他们可以深入展现自己经验和知识的演变过程,使自己显得更平易近人,从而更有可能激发他人想要了解更多的愿望。

transcript.text: The U.S. was founded by successive waves of immigrants, and immigrants are still contributing to America today—statistics prove it.
transcript.zh: 美国是由一波又一波的移民建立起来的,移民至今仍在为美国做出贡献——统计数据证明了这一点。

transcript.text: On two key measures of financial performance, immigrants outperform native-born Americans.
transcript.zh: 在衡量财务表现的两个关键指标上,移民的表现优于本土出生的美国人。

transcript.text: First, they are more likely to be entrepreneurs. From 1996 to 2016, the pace at which immigrants started businesses was double that of U.S.-born individuals. Immigrants aren't just becoming entrepreneurs more frequently. They're often succeeding. Over 40% of Fortune 500 companies had a founder who was either an immigrant or the child of one.
transcript.zh: 首先,他们更有可能成为企业家。从1996年到2016年,移民创业的速度是美国本土出生者的两倍。移民不仅更频繁地成为企业家,而且往往取得成功。超过40%的财富500强企业的创始人是移民或移民子女。

transcript.text: Another key measure of financial strength is debt level. Immigrants do better in this area too. Immigrants use credit less often for purchasing cars, homes or starting businesses. This results in significantly lower levels of debt than native-born Americans. For example, 34% of Americans born in Latin America report no credit card or installment loan debt. This can be compared to just 19% of the general population.
transcript.zh: 另一个衡量财务实力的关键指标是负债水平。移民在这方面也表现更好。移民较少使用信贷购买汽车、房屋或创业,因此其负债水平显著低于本土出生的美国人。例如,34%的拉丁美洲出生的美国人表示没有信用卡或分期贷款债务,而整体人口中这一比例仅为19%。

transcript.text: Why are immigrants doing so well? The values and habits they bring from their own homelands help explain some of the success.
transcript.zh: 为什么移民表现如此出色?他们从祖国带来的价值观和习惯有助于解释部分成功原因。

transcript.text: Unemployment tends to be higher in developing countries. That means more people must become entrepreneurs. Credit is also scarcer in most developing countries. This means individuals must save more in order to achieve their goals, or they borrow money from friends and family rather than a bank. That means less debt and potentially better credit outcomes when they reach the U.S.
transcript.zh: 发展中国家的失业率往往更高,这意味着更多人必须成为企业家。在大多数发展中国家,信贷也更加稀缺,这意味着个人必须储蓄更多才能实现目标,或者从朋友和家人而非银行借钱,这意味着更少的债务,并且在他们到达美国时可能获得更好的信用结果。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For the past four decades, the leader of Formula One car racing, one of the biggest annual sporting series in the world, was Bernie Ecclestone, a former motorcycle parts dealer who built it into an international presence essentially on his own.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: A skilled backroom operator who speaks without a filter, Ecclestone said often that in his opinion, the sport was at its best when he was allowed to act as "a dictator."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Yet now the dictator is gone. After an American company, Liberty Media, acquired the Formula One competition recently, Chase Carey—a former executive with Fox Broadcasting Company and DirecTV who by his own admission is not a fierce racing fan—was named to replace Ecclestone and to try to renovate the organization's management, reach and ambition.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Among the goals, Carey said in an interview on Tuesday, is one that just about every global sport seems interested in chasing: increasing interest in the United States. "People have said we're going to 'Americanize' it," Carey said. "And we're not going to do that totally. But realistically, there are some elements of Americanization that the sport could use."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: While Formula One commands enormous audiences throughout much of the world, many American sports fans know it as that other motorsport, the one that is not Nascar(纳斯卡车赛). Formula One teams race far more technologically advanced vehicles around tracks all over the world—in magnificent events in places like Malaysia, Monaco, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates, and on tradition-rich tracks like Silverstone in England and Monza in Italy too.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The series has an annual race in Austin, Texas. But within "a few years," Carey said, he plans to bring another to a destination American city, like New York, Los Angeles, Miami or Las Vegas. Carey's ambitious plan is two-fold: first, change the business model of Formula One, which he said was a "one-man show" under Ecclestone that had a largely narrow vision when it came to negotiating partnership deals; and second, alter the way fans experience the sport, both in person and remotely, so that connections between the audience and people within the series are easier to make.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Increased digital access for fans, a more behind-the-scenes experience for broadcast viewers and innovation in areas like virtual reality—what is it like to speed around a track inside a Ferrari?—are among the possibilities. "The sport has clearly been underserved," Carey said. "It doesn't do anything digitally. There's no marketing. It doesn't tell any stories. The goal in this is to make the fans connect to the live experience as much as possible, and the tools you have to do that, we're not using at all."

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The larger question, though, is a familiar one: Is there room for Formula One in the ever-crowded sports landscape of the United States? Opinions vary, particularly because viewing habits among consumers continue to evolve. John Bloom, a professor at Shippensburg University who has studied American sports history, said the biggest challenge for any sport trying to increase its presence in the United States was framing itself in a way that had lasting appeal. "Sports generally become popular in some way because they establish a narrative," Bloom said. "When I think of motorsports in the U.S., what we all think of is Nascar, and the narrative of Nascar is sort of rural, white, working-class Americans, mostly in the South, connecting with the atmosphere of those races. That's the narrative. When I think of the narrative of Formula One, it's a very different kind of audience."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: That difference, Carey said, is significant. While some might immediately link Formula One to Nascar in terms of American growth, Carey said Formula One's brand research had indicated there was very little crossover; rather, Formula One fans generally cite other so-called elite events, like Wimbledon or the Ryder Cup, as competitions they enjoy. "Other than they're both cars, the Nascar fan base is a very different fan base," Carey said. "It's a very regional fan base. Formula One is a global, famous brand of stars. These are machines that shock and awe you."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Carey's background is in deal making and innovation. At Fox Broadcasting Company, he was a top advisor for years, known for his skill in helping to lead the launch of the company into sports, as well as the start of Fox News Channel. After going to DirecTV, he positioned the satellite provider as a mainstream option in millions of households.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Now, after Liberty Media paid $4.4 billion to acquire Formula One, he is charged with making the investment pay off. "I think they can build Formula One in the U.S.," said Patrick Crakes, an executive at InVivo Media Group who spent 25 years at Fox Broadcasting Company before leaving in 2016 as a senior manager at Fox Sports. "People don't work on their cars anymore. They don't want that connection anymore. It's about technology and pushing the limits. It's about speed, danger and risk. And Formula One has that more than any other racing series."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: That is what hooked Carey, and he said he thought his experience was not unusual. He recalled attending Formula One's Monaco race last year and being overwhelmed by the ceremony leading up to the event, the way the race charmed the city for days ahead of the start. In his mind, it felt like a Super Bowl(超级碗橄榄球赛).

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Then, on race day, he watched as the cars rocketed out of a tunnel and went screaming toward a tight turn with the city's harbor and the Mediterranean Sea in the background framing the scene. He was fascinated. "You can't help but be awed," he said, "and I think that feeling can be translated to the viewer."

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: He added: "The broader sport is a little too inward-looking, and we need to be more open. In some ways, I'm glad to be coming from the outside. The guys who are in the sport forever are sitting there saying: 'We can't do that. We can't do that because it's never been done that way.'"

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The traditional school year, with three months of vacation every summer, was first implemented when America was an agricultural society and the summer months were needed for farm work. Since then, we've completely changed as a nation. Students no longer spend summers farming, but they aren't in school, either. The average American student receives 13 weeks off from school each calendar year-with about 11 of those during the summer. Few other countries have more than seven weeks off in a school calendar.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: With the U.S. lagging behind other countries in academics, it's time to consider year-round schooling. One benefit of this change is that students will not fall victim to the "summer slide," or the well-documented phenomenon where students forget some of the knowledge they have acquired when too much time is taken off from school. Decades of research shows that it can take from 8 to 13 weeks at the beginning of every school year for students to get back to where they were before the summer holiday.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: But year-round schooling isn't just about academics. Teachers and students experience a closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the absence of any long-term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment. These closer bonds and greater attachment pay off. Research shows that students in year-round schools are more self-confident and feel more positive about their schooling experience.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: But don't kids need time to relax? Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside. The problem with this argument is that most children aren't playing outside or even spending time with other kids. While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The U.S. has changed from a farming economy to a knowledge- and innovation-based economy, so it makes sense for the school year to change as well.
